Calculus 7: Complex Functions¶

A Function can take and return complex numbers, and the calculus operators follow. After this chapter you can build and evaluate complex functions with native scalars, take their Wirtinger derivatives, tell holomorphic from non-holomorphic functions, and use the ordinary operators on complex functions of a real parameter.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program.

The mental model¶

  • One graph, real or complex. The same traced body evaluates at real and complex points; a complex scalar is passed directly.

  • Two derivatives. wirtinger is ∂/∂z and conjugate_wirtinger is ∂/∂z̄; the function is holomorphic where the second is zero.

  • Principal branches. log, sqrt and fractional pow return the principal value, with the cut on the negative real axis.

  • Real parameters use the ordinary operators. differential and integral accept complex functions of a real variable.

Entry point

Purpose

math::function(std::complex<double>)

a complex constant

conj(), real(), imag(), abs(), angle()

parts of a complex number

operators::wirtinger(z, order)

∂/∂z

operators::conjugate_wirtinger(z, order)

∂/∂z̄

Programs¶

  • Complex values

  • Wirtinger derivatives

  • Real parameters and integrals

Checklist¶

  1. A complex literal such as 2.0 + 1i combines with a Function directly; math::function(c) makes a complex constant on its own.

  2. Read the conjugate derivative first: if it is zero the function is holomorphic and wirtinger is the usual derivative.

  3. Expect the principal branch from log, sqrt and fractional powers, and a jump across the negative real axis.

  4. real, imag, abs and angle return real values stored with a zero imaginary part.
